Register a new applicant

Self-registration creates a pending account that holds the requested role and Network as a preference, not a grant.

POST/Register
Expected
201 — status: pending, with the new id
Actual
201 · status=pending · id=17
  1. TestA1 · Register a new applicant
  2. ExercisesPOST /Register
  3. Implemented in3 source locations
  4. Checked byregister_applicant()
  5. ResultPassed
How it works
The handler bcrypt-hashes the password off the event loop, then inserts the row with role='pending' and status='pending' and writes an audit event in the same transaction. A previously rejected username is re-used by updating that row instead of inserting.
Inputs
A validated RestrictedRegistrationRequest: username rules, password strength and an assignable requested_role are enforced by the Pydantic model before the handler runs.
Behaviour
No PostgreSQL role is created. pending maps to no group role, so the account can do nothing yet.
What the test verifies
201 with status: pending and an id.
Depends on
Migrations 002 (password, status), 005 (dataset_id), 007 (requested_role) and 003 (AuditLog).

Review the pending queue

The admin user list shows the applicant as pending, with no effective role and never the password hash.

GET/Users
Expected

How it works
An administrator-only query returns every row ordered by id. The password column is stripped before serialising, and the internal pending role sentinel is reported as null.
Inputs
An administrator token.
Behaviour
Ordering by primary key keeps positions stable: an UPDATE writes a new row version elsewhere in the heap.
What the test verifies
role: null, status: pending, the requested Network and role, no password key, and ascending ids.
Depends on
set_role() switches to the administrator group role for the read.

Approve the applicant

An administrator grants a role (defaulting to the requested one) and a Network scope, which must name an existing Network.

PATCH/Users/{target_user_id}/policy-approval
Expected
200 — granted_role: viewer, status becomes active
Actual
200 · granted_role=viewer · dataset_id=acsot · status=active
  1. TestA4 · Approve the applicant
  2. ExercisesPATCH /Users/{target_user_id}/policy-approval
  3. Implemented in2 source locations
  4. Checked byapprove_applicant()
  5. ResultPassed
How it works
Inside one transaction the handler locks the pending row, resolves the role, validates dataset_id against the Network table, activates the account and writes an ADMIN_APPROVAL audit event.
Inputs
AdminApprovalRequest with optional role and dataset_id.
Behaviour
A rejected applicant cannot be approved directly (400); an unknown Network name is refused (400) so a scope can never silently match nothing.
What the test verifies
200 with granted_role: viewer, and the row reads role: viewer, status: active.
Depends on
NETWORK=1 enables the Network-name check.

Prove the RBAC boundary

A viewer asking for the user list is refused.

GET/Users

How it works
The handler raises InsufficientPrivilegeError for any caller whose live role is not administrator; the error is mapped to 401 with an explicit message.
Inputs
The viewer's token.

Beyond this check, the user group role also has SELECT on "User" revoked, so the data is protected at the database even if the check were removed.

401 with Insufficient privileges.
Depends on
get_current_user supplies the live role.

Refresh the token

Exchanges a still-valid token for a fresh one with a new expiry.

POST/Refresh
Expected
200 — a new access_token
Actual
200 · fresh access_token, accepted on the next call
  1. TestA7 · Refresh the token
  2. ExercisesPOST /Refresh
  3. Implemented in3 source locations
  4. Checked byrefresh_token()
  5. ResultPassed
How it works
The handler reads the bearer header itself, refuses a token already on the Redis deny-list, decodes it, and signs a new one with the same sub and role. With REDIS=1 the old token is added to the deny-list.
Inputs
Authorization: Bearer <token>.
Behaviour
A malformed header is 400, an undecodable token is 400, a revoked one is 401.
What the test verifies
200 and a new token that the next call accepts.
Depends on
Redis only for revoking the old token.

Change the role

An administrator re-assigns an active user's role; the change applies on that user's very next request.

PATCH/Users/{user_id}/role
Expected
204 — GET /Users shows role: editor
Actual
204 · role is now editor
  1. TestA8 · Change the role
  2. ExercisesPATCH /Users/{user_id}/role
  3. Implemented in3 source locations
  4. Checked bychange_role()
  5. ResultPassed
How it works
One UPDATE of the role column. No PostgreSQL role is created, altered or granted: the next request's set_role() simply maps the new value to its group role.
Inputs
RoleUpdateRequest with role and/or dataset (at least one required).
Behaviour
Pending users must be activated instead (400); demoting the last administrator is refused (409); an unknown Network is refused (400).
What the test verifies
204 and the new role in the user list.
Depends on
get_current_user re-reading role live, so no token rotation is needed.

Log out

Logout is acknowledged; the token is revoked only when Redis is enabled.

POST/Logout
Expected
200 — {"message": "Successfully logged out"}
Actual
200 · REDIS=0: acknowledged, token not revoked until it expires
  1. TestA10 · Log out
  2. ExercisesPOST /Logout
  3. Implemented in3 source locations
  4. Checked bylogout()
  5. ResultPassed
How it works
The handler decodes the token for its expiry and, when REDIS=1, stores it in Redis with a TTL that ends exactly when the token would have expired. get_current_user and /Refresh consult that list first.
Inputs
Authorization: Bearer <token>.
Behaviour
Without Redis there is no deny-list, so the call is an acknowledgement only. Deactivation (A12) is the revocation path that works regardless.
What the test verifies
200 and the documented behaviour for the running REDIS setting.
Depends on
REDIS and the Redis container.

Start the external login

The login route stores the requested Network and role in the server session and redirects to the provider.

GET/auth/{provider}/login
Expected
302 — redirect to the provider's authorize page
Actual
302 → provider /authorize (state + nonce set)

How it works
A redirect has no body, so dataset_id and requested_role are kept in the signed server session until the callback. Authlib builds the authorize URL with state (CSRF) and nonce (replay protection).
Inputs
Path provider, optional dataset_id and requested_role (validated against assignable roles).
Behaviour
Only providers with both client id and secret configured are registered; others are 404 (B4).
What the test verifies
302 to the provider's /authorize with state and nonce.
Depends on
*_CLIENT_ID / *_CLIENT_SECRET. The automated run uses the bundled fake OpenID provider.

Data visibility and Network scoping

What each role can read and change once authenticated, enforced by PostgreSQL row-level security rather than by the API.

Passed C1

The access matrix is installed

Every role's access comes from a fixed set of row-level-security policies written once for the deployment.

SQLpg_policies
RoleReference tables¹DatastreamObservation/Policies · /Commits
no token401401401401
viewerread allread, own Networkread, own Network401
editorread all · create; change existing only if unscopedread + write, own Networkread + write, own Network401
sensor / obs_managerread all · own Location updatesread, own Networkappend (sensor) · full (obs_manager)401
qcread allread, own Networkread + update quality401
customnothing until granted (Part D)as grantedas granted401
administratoreverything (table owner, RLS bypassed)everythingeverything200

¹ Thing, Sensor, Location, HistoricalLocation, ObservedProperty, FeaturesOfInterest, Network. Local and external identities behave identically: policies read only role and Network scope, never the auth provider.

Expected
All rbac_* policies present; RLS enabled on the scoped tables
Actual
42 rbac_* policies · RLS on 9 tables
  1. TestC1 · The access matrix is installed
  2. ExercisesSQL pg_policies
  3. Implemented in4 source locations
  4. Checked bystatic_policy_set()
  5. ResultPassed
How it works
Migration 006 generates one SELECT policy per group role and table, plus write policies per role. Several application roles share a group role (viewer, editor and custom all run as user), so predicates tell them apart through current_app_user_role().
Inputs
custom.network at migration time decides whether the Network predicates are generated.
Behaviour
Policies are static: no policy is ever created per user for the built-in roles. The number of PostgreSQL roles stays fixed at seven no matter how many users exist.
What the test verifies
The expected policy names exist and RLS is enabled on the scoped tables.
Depends on
set_role() on every request, and the helper functions.

A viewer sees only its own Network

Two users on the same PostgreSQL role see different rows, decided by their Network grant.

GET/Datastreams
Expected
200 — exactly the Datastreams of the viewer's Network; admin sees all
Actual
viewer(acsot) sees 10 · admin sees 20
  1. TestC3 · A viewer sees only its own Network
  2. ExercisesGET /Datastreams
  3. Implemented in4 source locations
  4. Checked byviewer_sees_own_network()
  5. ResultPassed
How it works
The read runs in a transaction that first calls set_role(): SET LOCAL ROLE "user" plus app.current_user_id. The Datastream SELECT policy then keeps rows whose network_id equals current_app_user_network_id(), which resolves the caller's Network name to an id.
Inputs
The viewer's token; the Network name stored on their row.
Behaviour
A Network name that matches nothing yields no rows (fail-closed). An unscoped viewer (dataset_id null) sees every Network.
What the test verifies
The viewer's ids equal the Network's ids from Setup; admin sees at least both Networks.
Depends on
NETWORK=1; the administrator group owns the tables and bypasses RLS.

A viewer cannot write, even in its Network

The row is visible, but no write policy matches a viewer, so the update affects nothing and is reported as 403.

PATCH/Datastreams({datastream_id})
Expected
403 — Insufficient privileges to update this Datastream.
Actual
403 · Insufficient privileges to update this Datastream.
  1. TestC4 · A viewer cannot write, even in its Network
  2. ExercisesPATCH /Datastreams({datastream_id})
  3. Implemented in3 source locations
  4. Checked byviewer_cannot_write()
  5. ResultPassed
How it works
The existence probe succeeds because SELECT is allowed. The UPDATE then matches zero rows under RLS, update_entity returns False, and the handler turns that into an explicit 403 instead of a silent 200.
Inputs
Viewer token, a visible Datastream id, a JSON patch body.
Behaviour
PostgreSQL does not raise on an UPDATE filtered away by RLS; checking the affected row is what makes the refusal visible.
What the test verifies
403 with the explicit message.
Depends on
Only editor has a write policy on Datastream in the user group.

An editor is blocked outside its Network

Creating into another Network fails the policy check; another Network's rows look like they do not exist.

POST/Datastreams · PATCH /Datastreams({id})
Expected
POST → 403 Insufficient privileges. · PATCH → 404 Datastream not found.
Actual
POST into other Network → 403 · PATCH other Network's row → 404
  1. TestC7 · An editor is blocked outside its Network
  2. ExercisesPOST /Datastreams · PATCH /Datastreams({id})
  3. Implemented in3 source locations
  4. Checked byeditor_blocked_outside_network()
  5. ResultPassed
How it works
The INSERT violates the policy's WITH CHECK, PostgreSQL raises InsufficientPrivilegeError, and a global handler maps it to 403. For the PATCH, the existence probe is a SELECT that RLS already filters, so the row is simply not found.
Inputs
Editor token and a Network or row outside its scope.
Behaviour
RLS hides out-of-scope rows entirely; there is no “exists but forbidden” signal to leak their existence.
What the test verifies
403 for the insert and 404 for the update.
Depends on
Registered exception handlers in the app.

Observation counts follow the Network scope

Observation has no Network column; its scope flows down from its parent Datastream.

GET/Observations?$count=true
Expected
200 — @iot.count equals the viewer's Network's observations
Actual
200 · @iot.count=20160 (whole table: 40320)
  1. TestC8 · Observation counts follow the Network scope
  2. ExercisesGET /Observations?$count=true
  3. Implemented in2 source locations
  4. Checked byobservation_counts_scoped()
  5. ResultPassed
How it works
The Observation policy tests datastream_id = ANY(current_app_user_datastream_ids()). A function returning an array is used instead of an IN (SELECT …) subquery because TimescaleDB's SkipScan aborts on the subplan a subquery creates, which made $count fail with a 500.
Inputs
Viewer token, $count=true.
Behaviour
An unknown Network yields an empty array, never NULL, so the predicate stays fail-closed.
What the test verifies
The count equals the Setup count for the viewer's Network, not the whole table.
Depends on
Observation is a TimescaleDB hypertable.

Policies and commits are administrator-only

Neither table has a per-user or per-Network column, so both are restricted outright.

GET/Policies · /Commits
Expected
viewer 401 · admin 200 (both endpoints)
Actual
Policies 401/200 · Commits 401/200 (viewer/admin)
  1. TestC9 · Policies and commits are administrator-only
  2. ExercisesGET /Policies · /Commits
  3. Implemented in3 source locations
  4. Checked byadmin_only_metadata()
  5. ResultPassed
How it works
Both handlers raise InsufficientPrivilegeError for any non-administrator before building a query. The Commits router is only mounted when versioning is on.
Inputs
A token.
Behaviour
Filtering would be meaningless: policies and commits describe the whole deployment.
What the test verifies
401 for a viewer and 200 for admin on both.
Depends on
VERSIONING=1 for Commits.

An external identity behaves identically

A Google-authenticated viewer and a local viewer in the same Network get the same answers.

GET/Datastreams · /Observations · PATCH
Expected
Identical counts, 403 on own rows, 404 on other rows
Actual
identical on datastreams, observation count, 403 own, 404 other
  1. TestC10 · An external identity behaves identically
  2. ExercisesGET /Datastreams · /Observations · PATCH
  3. Implemented in2 source locations
  4. Checked byexternal_matches_local()
  5. ResultPassed
How it works
Nothing downstream reads auth_provider: get_current_user returns role and status, set_role() maps the role, and policies read the Network grant. Both identity types therefore take the same path.
Inputs
The external token from B3 and a local viewer in the same Network.
Behaviour
The only designed difference is that external identities cannot set a local password.
What the test verifies
Datastream ids, observation count and both PATCH outcomes are equal.
Depends on
B3. A scripted version covers six roles × 26 operations (run_auth_parity.py).

Grant a mixed rule

One call creates one RLS policy per operation, so read and write scope can differ for the same user.

POST/Policies
Expected

  3. Implemented in2 source locations
  4. Checked bygrant_mixed_rule()
  5. ResultPassed
How it works
create_policies resolves the users (all must have role custom), then emits CREATE POLICY <name>_<table>_<op> … TO "user" whose predicate is current_app_user_id() = ANY(<ids>) AND (<condition>). Identifiers are quoted and conditions are screened for unsafe tokens.
Inputs
users, name, and permissions.policy keyed by table then operation.
Behaviour
Built-in role types return 200 without creating anything; they are already covered by static policies. A duplicate name is 409.
What the test verifies
201 and both policy names present in GET /Policies.
Depends on
current_app_user_id() from the session helpers.

The custom user's token.

Separate policies per operation are what make the split possible.

The visible set, both PATCH outcomes and the 404.

D2's policies.
